blocks.intro: Gas fireplaces were a common feature in Algonquin homes built in the 1990s and 2000s.

items.body: Original pilots, valves and thermopiles wear out, but most parts are still available.
Homeowners who never use a wood fireplace often switch to gas logs for push-button heat.
Direct-vent fireplaces vent through a cap on the outside wall. Snow and nests can block it.
Keep a working CO detector on every level.

blocks.h2: Gas Fireplace Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: Can you install gas logs in my wood-burning fireplace?
items.preview: Yes, if the chimney is sound.
items.answer: Yes. We run the gas line, install the logs and valve and test everything. The chimney needs to be in good shape and drawing well.

items.q: How often should my gas fireplace be serviced?
items.preview: Once a year, in early fall.
items.answer: Once a year, ideally in September or October.

items.q: Why won't my fireplace stay lit?
items.preview: Usually a weak thermopile or thermocouple.
items.answer: Usually a thermopile or thermocouple that can't hold the gas valve open anymore. It's a common, fixable repair.

items.q: What if I smell gas near the fireplace?
items.preview: Leave and call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside.
items.answer: Leave without touching switches. Call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside, then call us once it's safe.

items.q: What does gas fireplace repair cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on what failed. The price comes first.
items.answer: It depends on the part and the fireplace model. We quote a flat rate before we start.
